messages:
sre-oncall: alert: elevated apiserver READ p95 in eu-central1 since 09:05UTC. controller-manager leader churning, gpu-provisioner backlog climbing.

anil: checking etcd and node disks.

maria: seeing nvme i/o errors and long fsyncs on etcd nodes. sample: 
`kernel: blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1`

chris: gpu queue ~1800 pending, provision rate dropped from 50/s -> 10/s. cost pressure if we replace many nodes.

infra-bot: ALERT: apiserver_read_latency_p95 eu-central1 triggered

anil: root cause looks like WAL fsync stalls causing apiserver read timeouts and ctrlmgr lease timeouts -> leader flips.

maria: ctrlmgr logs: "failed to renew lease: operation timed out".

chris: mitigation plan: 1) throttle onboarding jobs, 2) label eu-central nodes lowprio and divert new GPU provisioning to west-eu canary, 3) bump etcd WAL retry/backoff and consider moving leader.

sre-oncall: execute 1+3 now, Chris prepare diversion. I'll notify customers.

anil: applied etcd fsync backoff tweak; cordoning one NVMe host for healthcheck and promoting a follower leader candidate.

maria: increasing leader-election timeouts in kube-controller-manager (30s->60s lease) and rolling shards staggered.

infra-bot: CMD: `kubectl get pods -n gpu-provisioning`
infra-bot: ```
NAME                      READY   STATUS
gpu-provisioner-0         1/1     Running
gpu-provisioner-1         0/1     CrashLoopBackOff
```

chris: applying node label patch for scheduling preference to west-eu; will spin 5-node canary then ramp.

sre-oncall: monitor p95 for 20m. If re-spike -> escalate to incident. Post-incident: NVMe firmware check, consider higher-iops instance types for etcd leaders, add admission rate-limit for bursty gpu requests, cost analysis for diversion.

maria: opening follow-up ticket and assigning owners.

sre-oncall: thanks, keep updates brief here."
